conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the scientific consensus rejects the claim, stating that rigorous reviews show abortion does not increase breast cancer risk and that opposing assertions are false.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
The claim that abortion increases breast cancer risk is not supported by mainstream scientific evidence and is considered false by the major bodies that have systematically reviewed the research.

**What the major scientific reviews say:** In February 2003, the National Cancer Institute convened over 100 leading experts on pregnancy and breast cancer to review population-based, clinical, and animal studies. Their conclusion, still maintained on the NCI's site, found no causal relationship between induced or spontaneous abortion and breast cancer risk (https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/abortion-miscarriage-risk). This finding has been reaffirmed by later reviews: a 2018 report from the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine concluded abortion does not affect breast cancer risk, and the American Cancer Society states that "higher-quality studies have generally found no link between abortions and breast cancer risk" (https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html). The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and Susan G. Komen similarly state the evidence does not support a link, noting earlier studies suggesting one were methodologically flawed—often relying on retrospective self-reporting subject to recall bias (https://www.komen.org/breast-cancer/facts-statistics/research-studies/topics/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk/).

**Where the contrary claims come from:** Sources asserting a link—such as the Coalition on Abortion/Breast Cancer, Illinois Family Institute, and similar advocacy sites—are generally politically motivated, anti-abortion organizations rather than independent scientific or medical bodies. Wikipedia's summary notes this hypothesis "is at odds with mainstream scientific opinion and is rejected by major medical professional organizations" despite continuing to circulate as pseudoscience (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion–breast_cancer_hypothesis).

**Conclusion:** Your skepticism is well-founded. The scientific consensus, based on the most rigorous, large-scale reviews, is that abortion does not increase breast cancer risk.
